# `response-header-removed`

Response header removed (error if it was required)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `warn` |
| **Rule IDs** | `response-header-removed` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M3) |
| **Group** | Responses ([RULES.md section 6](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A response header was removed. An error if the header was `required`, otherwise a warning.

## Why this default

Clients that read it (e.g. a rate-limit or request-ID header) lose the value. A required header was promised, so clients may not check that it's there.

## Example

From test case [`response-header-removed`](../../test/cases/response-header-removed/): An optional response header removed is a warning.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          '200':
            description: ok
-           headers:
-             X-Rate-Limit:
-               schema:
-                 type: string
+           headers: {}
```

Findings:

- `response-header-removed` · warn · GET /pets

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

Options for this rule:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `required-severity` | `error` | Severity when the removed header was required. |

```yaml
rules:
  response-header-removed: warn
```

## How to fix

Keep sending the header until clients stop reading it.
